doc.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003

title: Church, large family, violin and Uncle Ben Holliman's Eubie Blake story
summary: Ridley cites the church, his big family and early violin as pivot points; he tells Eubie Blake's pool hall story via his uncle.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well I think that there are little pivot points that sort of set the tone for what my destiny — if I can use that word — was to be. I think my spiritual values came from the time that I was an altar boy in the African Methodist Episcopal Church. My brother and I, my brother that’s next to me, we were both at an early age, seven years old or something like that. And my mother was originally a Baptist so I came up through that whole African- American tradition of Baptist church and then the African-American Episcopal Church. So certain spiritual values, and then my family, I came from a very large family. My mother came from a family of 13 kids. So the get-togethers at my grandparents’ home was always like a mini-United Nations. And I became very early aware of the differences in personalities and people like this. So a combination of those kind of spiritual aspects and also recognizing the differences that exist among people. And as I’ve grown older you know you realize all of these things transcend ethnicity or the limitations of ethnicity, you realize that human beings are human beings. And you begin to just look and see what are those things and you do a quick study on being able to have insight into understanding that and how to not be unnerved by certain types of situations. I started playing music when I was three years old, playing the violin. In fact I had like a little tiny violin it was about that size. And unfortunately I had some pictures, and I like to think that they were cute, everybody says that they were cute, but I think a lot of them were lost in memorabilia that my parents had in our home in Indianapolis and so it’s up here. So God knows. But the music thing, and then I had an uncle, Ben Holliman, who was a
gentleman who befriended Hoagy Carmichael. In fact my Uncle Ben always told me that the major part of the song “Stardust” was his.
A lot of people are not aware of this. And Hoagy was very close to my uncle for all of his life.
And your uncle was a musician?

Yes. He was an entertainer and he was a good friend of Eubie Blake. In fact Eubie Blake told me stories about how they met. Eubie was traveling through Indianapolis, Indiana and Eubie was kind of down on his finances. So he went to the local pool hall and he was an excellent pool shark. And he kind of played down his ability and he told these guys, “Yeah well I’d like to shoot a few rounds” and they set up the limits for whatever the wager would be. And so he proceeded to just kind of take it easy and then after a while he immediately started running the table on them. And these guys were ready to jump up and guys were pulling out their knives and everything, talking about, “We’re going to cut this guy.” And my uncle knew all these guys and being that Eubie was a stranger just passing through, you know they didn’t know who this guy was and they say oh this guy comes in and is going to set us up and take all our money. And so my uncle saved him from these guys. Which I thought was a great story.
He never would have reached a hundred.
